# Stellix

A synth by The Decipherist with no wall of knobs: four sound slots, shaped by touching planets and moons in a 3D space,
drawn natively in C++. Every rule that applies only to one kind of file is in `.claude/rules/` and loads with that file.

## Read first

| | |
|---|---|
| `docs/stellix-spec.md` | The spec. **Section 0 is set in stone**; in 5.1 the seed (`docs/research/stellix-seed.json`) wins over the quoted numbers |
| `docs/stellix-layers.md` | The build sheet for the SOUND and MIXER layers (2026-10-29); spec 3.1, 3.2 and moon spec 2a to 2c win where it is shorter |
| `build.md` | Where the build is. Read it at the start of every session; nothing is worked on unless it is IN PROGRESS there |
| `bugs.md`, `workflow-bugs.md` | Every bug, logged before it is fixed |
| `design/reference/stellix-concept-v1.png` | The approved look. The spec wins where they differ (STELLIX not GRAVITY, no chevrons, invented names are placeholders) |
| `docs/workorders/stellix-workorder.md` | The plan as written for apprack2: its items are build.md's steps, its machinery is not used here |
| `docs/laws.md`, `docs/licences.md` | Where Stellix leaves a house law (with the user's yes), and what came from where |
| `~/projects/eproms/synth-design.md` | The house lessons log; a lesson for the next synth goes there |

## Set in stone (spec 0; never changed, each held by a hook or a gate)

1. Everything is drawn natively, in code, live. 2. **Nothing is ever pre-rendered**: no image file in the source or
resources, no export or render step (`source_rules.py`, pre-commit). 3. Picture checks come from the app itself, never a
browser (`browser-guard`). 4. **Formulas by default**: the one RANDOM source is the world's seeded generator
(`lib/world/include/stellix/world/random_source.h`), off in INIT and every factory patch, never on a sound-character moon
(`source_rules.py`, `records_gate.py`, `bank_census.py`). 5. **Reset is iron clad**: every piece of state is a
`stellix::State` with its start, so a state without one does not compile; a patch load is a reset, then apply.
6. The sound is shaped in the space: no knob or slider shapes the sound.

## Non-negotiables

- **Standalone only. arm64 only**: no Intel build, no Rosetta, no VST3 until the user calls for it.
- **Performance is judged on an Apple M1 Pro (2021), never on this machine**. A probe's baseline is keyed
  by machine model (`sysctl hw.model`); a figure from any other model is printed and labelled, never judged.
- **TheDecipherist, private.** Every push and every `gh` names `$PERSONAL_GITHUB_TOKEN` on the command; it is never stored
  in a remote, a config or a file (`git-guard`). Commit author claude-packs.
- **One branch per step, every step merged and pushed, its start and finish in the log** (`tools/step.py`). Never commit to
  `main`, never `add -A`, never rebase, amend, force or delete a branch, never `--no-verify`.
- **No source file over 300 lines** (a hook refuses it). Split by what the code does.
- **Measure, never assume.** Every gate is seen red on its planted fault (`tools/plants.sh`) before anything is ticked.
- **Engines and effects come from Tabula 1's current main by copy-and-prove**, fingerprinted against their source first;
  never from apprack2, which is paused.
- **the user's other projects are open to read and update** (2026-10-31; WB-64 removed `project-guard`): no hook, rule or guard
  blocks them. In every repo: `git status` first, stage by explicit path (never `add -A`), never restore or checkout over
  uncommitted work, never commit to main, push to TheDecipherist with the token named and never stored (`git-guard` holds these
  wherever the command runs). Before writing in another project, check whether its own session is open, and say what changed in
  that project's own log.
- **Anything the spec leaves open goes to the user as a `d-n`** with the spec's recommendation, never decided by guessing.
- Stop only at a picture stop: the pictures beside the concept in `build/for-tim.md`.
- **A hook that blocks correct work is a red check** (WB-55): stop and report it with the exact message; never route around it
  (no code in an unrelated existing file, no file past 300 lines, no shell write). It is fixed first, with a selftest.

## Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `lib/world` | The world: coordinates only, the 240 Hz tick, the triple-buffered snapshot (no painter, no JUCE) |
| `lib/painter` | Everything drawn: the space, the columns, the keyboard band; reads only the snapshot |
| `lib/engines`, `lib/effects` | Sound engines and effects, copied from Tabula 1 and proved |
| `lib/app` | The standalone, the player and the scripted demo; JUCE is its own static library (`stellix_juce`) |
| `probes/` | Each probe its own executable, with a `--selftest` that plants its fault |
| `data/records`, `data/bank` | Moon records (what RANDOM may reach), the bank |
| `tools/` | `step.py`, `build.sh`, `plants.sh`, `gates/`, `hooks/` (the pre-commit) |
| `out/` | The build (Ninja, ccache); never committed |
| `build/` | `for-tim.md`, `pictures/` (rendered by the app, never read by a build step), `evidence/` |

## Commands

Build, test, run and plants are in the generated "Project commands" section below. The rest:

```
bash tools/hooks/install.sh                        # once per clone: the pre-commit
python3 tools/step.py start S<n> "task" | save "note" | check | finish S<n> --proof "..." | land --proof "..."
python3 tools/next_number.py bug|law|wb --take "title"   # the only way to get a B-, L- or WB- number
source ~/.env && git push https://x-access-token:$PERSONAL_GITHUB_TOKEN@github.com/TheDecipherist/stellix.git <branch>
```

Plain language with the user, conclusion first. Times carry date, time and zone, America/New_York. Never claim something works
that has not been built, opened and measured.

## Project layout

<constraints>
Always do:
- Put every kind of thing in its one place. The rules, checks and skills for it load only there:
- The other folders:
  - `data/`: data/records (fixed ids, moons) and data/bank (factory patches)
  - `docs/`: spec, delay spec, laws, licences, research, work order (plan and logs at the root: build.md, bugs.md, workflow-bugs.md)
  - `lib/app/`: the standalone, processor, editor, player, demo and the one launch function (launch.cpp)
  - `lib/app/gates/`: the gate readers: the window's STELLIX_LOOK_* readings (state and steps), linked only by the gate build StellixGates (stellix_gate_readers), never by the shipped Stellix.app (F9)
  - `lib/app/tabula/`: a COPY TREE (kind copy): Tabula 1's PIANO loader, bridge and prebuild tool (they use JUCE, which the engines may not see), copied unchanged by tools/copy_tabula.py; read-only as every copy tree
  - `lib/effects/`: effects and dynamics: delay, EQ, compressor, limiter (S11a-S11d)
  - `lib/engines/`: SlotSound and Tabula 1's voice, copied and proved (src/tabula is changed only under null tests, L8 and d-14, each changed part pinned by tools/copy_tabula.py --check)
  - `lib/engines/src/own/`: PROMOTED files (kind own): copied files that measured identical to their source, moved out of the copy tree by tools/copy_promote.py into Stellix's own code, each with its .origin record (origin line, licence row, the measurement); these may be changed
  - `lib/engines/src/tabula/`: a COPY TREE (kind copy): Tabula 1's voice, effects and dspblocks files and PIANO's recordings, copied unchanged by tools/copy_tabula.py; read-only (L8): every file has its origin line (repo, commit, SHA-256, licence row), changed only under null tests and pinned
  - `lib/gpu/`: the Dawn (WebGPU) foundation: the shared instance and device, the render thread, the CAMetalLayer surface, the HDR target and tonemap, the off-screen path, embedded WGSL (F6); lib/gpu/harness holds the test harness's GPU readbacks (pictures, opt-in timestamps), never run in a normal frame
  - `lib/painter/`: everything drawn: scene, camera, card, GPU layer, shaders, the Painter facade
  - `lib/snapshot/`: the one shared snapshot header the painter reads (header-only)
  - `lib/world/`: the world: travellers, strikes, rebounds, PULL, walls, the snapshot ring, State and the seeded RandomSource
  - `probes/`: probe executables, each with --selftest, and the shot program (pictures, benches)
  - `tools/`: build.sh, step.py, gates/, hooks/, plants.sh and plants.d/, copy and compare tools
  - `tools/plants/`: planted-fault sources run by tools/plants.sh
- Ask the user before inventing a new folder. A new folder goes into `.claude/layout.json` first.
- When a hook, check or guard blocks work that is correct, stop and report its exact message. A blocking hook is a red check: fix the hook first, with a selftest, then continue.
- When a command is refused or fails, the step fails loudly. Never report a refused write or a failed command as done.
- claude-packs (`@thedecipherist/claude-packs`) is the source of truth for every rule, check, hook and skill used to build synths. A fix to one of them, or a lesson that should hold in every synth, is made in the kit, with its test, and comes here with `npx --no-install @thedecipherist/claude-packs update`, so every synth gets it. A project edits its installed copy only to try a fix before it goes into the kit.

Never do:
- Create source files outside these folders, or put a kind of thing anywhere but its place. The folder-law and placement-law hooks refuse both.
- Put drawing code in audio or world folders, or audio and world logic in the painter or UI folders.
- Edit files in `.claude/rules`, `.claude/checks` or `.claude/hooks` to get past a block. Fix the code, or ask the user to change the law.
- Route around a block: no override variables, no writing through the shell after a refusal, no parking files in a scratchpad, no putting new code into an unrelated existing file.
- Point at a document by line number. Cite a fixed anchor (`{#id}`) or a symbol name; lines move.
</constraints>

## Project commands

Skills and checks run these; use them, not the raw tools:
- build: `bash tools/build.sh build`
- test: `bash tools/build.sh test`
- test-one: `bash tools/build.sh test -R <name>`
- plants: `bash tools/plants.sh`
- run: `bash tools/build.sh run`
- step: `python3 tools/step.py status`
- cpu-gate: `bash tools/build.sh test -R stellix.cpu_gate`
- frame-bench: `stellix_shot --bench (built by `bash tools/build.sh build`)`
- picture-gates: `bash tools/build.sh test -R '_gate'`

Installed packs: base, audio-core, gpu-painter, stellix.
